claims.claim: Home collateral coverage (real estate value / mortgage debt) was 3.56x in 2026Q2.

anchors: The public sector holds most household debt, but holding a loan is not the same as losing on it. Most of the public book is mortgages, and in aggregate homes are worth 3.56× the mortgages against them. Borrowers' equity, private mortgage insurance and the GSEs' risk-transfer deals stand in front of the taxpayer; this site does not measure how much they absorb. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have been in federal conservatorship since 2008.

claims.claim: The public sector holds 86% of student loans.
claims.notes: Holdings, not guarantees: bank-held FFEL loans carried federal guarantees but are counted private.
anchors: The public sector holds 86% of student loans and 51% of all household debt with no collateral, up from 7% in 2007. Part of that is relabelling: before 2010 most student loans held by banks already carried a federal guarantee. The debt can't be repossessed, but it is hard to discharge and can be collected from wages and tax refunds, so losses depend on collection, not collateral.
